challenges.name: fake-scheduler
challenges.title: A virtual clock for view model tests
challenges.description: The courier signal banner (LIVE, STALE after 2 minutes without a location, OFFLINE after 3 more) was tested with real delays: the suite took four minutes and failed whenever CI was slow. The view model now schedules through a `Scheduler` interface, and the tests need a `FakeScheduler` that moves a virtual clock, the way `TestCoroutineScheduler` does in kotlinx-coroutines-test. The editor holds `FakeScheduler.kt` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: `after(delay, task)` queues the task at now + delay and returns a handle whose `cancel()` stops it for good; `advanceTimeBy(ms)` runs every live task due by now + ms in time order (tasks due at the same moment in the order they were scheduled), sets `now` to each task's own time before running it, also runs tasks that running tasks schedule if they fall due in the window, and leaves the clock at now + ms. The runner drives the real view model and a few labelled tasks on your scheduler and prints what happened at which virtual millisecond.
hints: Replay the banner by hand: a location at 0 queues a check at 120000; when it runs, the check queues the offline step at 120000 + 180000. What must `now` be while the check runs for that to come out right?
Look at how `advanceTimeBy` loops: pick one task, run it, pick again. The pick must skip cancelled tasks, look only at tasks due by the target, and break ties by the order they were queued (`seq`).

A fake for a timer wheel in a game loop: `fun tick(ms: Long) { val end = clock + ms; while (true) { val t = timers.filter { !it.dead && it.at <= end }.minWithOrNull(compareBy({ it.at }, { it.order })) ?: break; timers.remove(t); clock = t.at; t.fire() }; clock = end }`.

A new location cancels the pending STALE check
Tasks run in time order; equal times run in the order scheduled

task B 5000
task C 2000
advance 10000

tests.name: Tasks scheduled by running tasks run in the same advance when due

chain E 1000 500
advance 1200
task F 0
advance 0

[1000] E
[1000] D-next
[1200] F
